extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers interested in anthology curation and the Best American series (fans, aspiring anthology contributors, and general book readers)
extracted.subtask_description: A close-read/history of the Best American anthology series focusing on how editions are assembled, editorial roles, what kinds of pieces are selected, and factors that influence which series persist or end. Useful for understanding anthology selection standards and editorial taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series editor screening
rubrics_metrics.description: The series editor evaluates all of the submissions for the given year (which, according to Angeloro, can be in the thousands for the Short Stories book and the Essays book) and then passes along a large set of selections to the guest editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and gatekeeping role: initial filtering at large scale, determining the pool from which guest editors choose. Quoted phrasing: 'evaluates all of the submissions... and then passes along a large set of selections to the guest editor.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest editor final selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The guest editor then eventually chooses what they feel are the best pieces for the book, although they can always bounce ideas off of the series editor and discuss different pieces and their thoughts about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final curatorial judgment rests with the guest editor; selections reflect that editor's perspective and taste. Emphasis on subjective 'what they feel are the best pieces' and the possibility of consultation with the series editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Championing literary work over popular publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Founding aim: spotlight and champion the literary stories that were being overshadowed by more popular stories in magazines (Edward J. O'Brien's motivation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curation favors literary quality rather than mass-market popularity. The historical mission was to highlight 'literary' as opposed to 'popular' short fiction appearing in mainstream magazines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft qualities of strong personal essays
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong personal essays show 'the power of the personal essay' and often demonstrate effective pacing, structure, and the ability to 'pack so much in, in just a few pages.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical craft criteria to model or evaluate: tight pacing, clear structure, economical use of space, and emotional/argumentative potency. The author describes re-reading pieces to study 'pacing, the structure, and how they managed to pack so much in.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of contributors and publication sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Over the years there has been more diversity in the essays and pieces collected, including where the pieces were originally published; editors often include work from a broader range of outlets beyond prestige venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curators value geographic/publication diversity and inclusion of pieces from smaller or less-canonical venues (e.g., 'Orion' or 'The Bitter Southerner') as well as traditionally lauded outlets. The piece explicitly notes a preference for finding fantastic writers in lesser-known publications rather than another lauded writer from 'The New Yorker.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and timeliness of an edition
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors want the series to 'feel relevant' and some editions act as 'time capsules' of particular years (example: The Best American 2021 books felt like time capsules of 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An edition is judged by how well it captures the moment or speaks to contemporary concerns; perceived relevance can influence both selection and reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions to start/continue/discontinue series based on media landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not to continue a specific series is often a decision that mirrors the larger media landscape; they want the series to feel relevant, and that can change each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical/strategic criterion: publishers evaluate demand, topical relevance, and marketplace fit when deciding which themed series persist (explains discontinuation of some series like Nonrequired Reading and Comics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest editor identity and perspective as curatorial factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year a new guest editor is chosen—often well-known writers who bring a compelling perspective to the book and influence what they choose; some guest editors generate more excitement than others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors' reputations, tastes, and perspectives materially shape an edition's tone and selection; choice of guest editor can increase reader interest and affect the anthology's direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representativeness of a themed edition
rubrics_metrics.description: An edition should represent its field/topic well; the Travel 2021 edition is cited as the 'least representative iteration' and its discontinuation is noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation includes whether a themed volume feels representative of its topic across voices and subjects—failure to do so can lead to poor reception or discontinuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic selection and topical expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: The series has added and discontinued themed collections (Science and Nature, SFF, Food, Travel, etc.), and future topics may be added depending on interest (e.g., suggestions like Political Writing, Parenting, Tech, Children's/YA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curatorial and market-fit criterion: deciding which topical series to create or revive depends on reader interest, cultural relevance, and editorial capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial collaboration and iterative selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest editors can 'bounce ideas off of the series editor and discuss different pieces and their thoughts about them,' indicating collaborative decision-making in finalizing selections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is not purely unilateral; productive back-and-forth between series and guest editors can refine choices and improve the final lineup.
